clue.text: My iron forge melting contents of large Dorset fortification

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
to forge metal is to cast it

indicators.note: the inside of the word large melts away, leaving only its two ends

explanation.surface: A smith melts down iron in a forge, apparently with the help of something large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melting contents of' strips ARG from LARGE, leaving LE. CORFE CASTLE is a ruined castle in Dorset, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined castle at Corfe is a famous medieval stronghold in the Purbeck hills of that county.

clue.text: Senior bowled Henry out regularly

indicators.note: every other letter of bowled Henry is let out, the second, fourth and so on being kept

explanation.surface: An older cricketer called Henry has been bowled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out regularly' takes the even letters of BOWLED HENRY: O, L, D, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior person is one who is older in years or rank.

clue.text: Supporter hit part of car's cooling system

parts.note: a fan supports a team or star
to belt is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A supporter hits part of a car's engine.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber loop drives the radiator fan in many engines, so it belongs to the cooling equipment.

clue.text: Tempt California actress Angelina out of Italy

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: out of says the letter for Italy leaves the actress's surname

parts.note: Angelina Jolie is the Hollywood actress
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lure a Californian film star away from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cajole is to coax or wheedle someone, which is a gentle way to lure them.

clue.text: Horrid and nasty, terribly up itself

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words up itself are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of someone unpleasant and very conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges UP ITSELF. 'Up itself' is British slang for conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful person is malicious, mean and unkind, which matches horrid and nasty.

clue.text: Politician runs article featured in defamation

indicators.note: featured in means these pieces appear inside the word for defamation

parts.note: libel is written defamation
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A politician runs a story that turns out to be defamatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal is a member of a Liberal party, so a kind of political figure.

clue.text: Salad of fig, ham and lettuce that's popular in Covent Garden?

indicators.note: a salad tosses its ingredients together, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A salad of fig, ham and lettuce sold at Covent Garden market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad of' rearranges FIG HAM AND LETTUCE. Covent Garden, the old London market, is home to the Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera is a perennial favourite at the Royal Opera House, so a hit there.

clue.text: Plant small flower over heather

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the river's name is turned upwards

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Dee
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a small flower above the heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DEE into EED. 'flower' is the crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: A seedling is a young plant raised from seed.

clue.text: Son having a nap outside pub yard in birthday suit, soaking wet

indicators.note: outside says the napping word sits around the pub and yard

parts.note: kipping is slang for sleeping
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A son naps outside a pub's yard, apparently naked and drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming naked leaves you bare as on the day you were born and wet through.

clue.text: Tricked husband (a lecturer)

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A wife was deceived by her husband, who is a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is British idiom for teasing or fooling them.

clue.text: In Paris, I have left holiday escape at the Bastille?

parts.note: j'ai is French for I have
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A tourist in Paris leaves for a holiday at a historic site.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was a notorious Paris prison, so a breakout from it is a gaol escape.

clue.text: Somewhere on the Med, buried in west-facing chapel lies Rameau

indicators.note: west-facing in an across clue means reading right to left
buried in says the answer lies concealed within the run of words

explanation.surface: The composer Rameau lies buried in a chapel facing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried in' and 'west-facing' together give the letters of chapEL LIES RAMeau read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is the great French port on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Element of attack happening by air

indicators.note: by air means transmitted through the air as speech

parts.note: a raid on something is an attack happening to it

explanation.surface: An element of an attack that comes from the air, an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by air' signals that RAID ON, spoken, gives the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Giuseppe's first story about old ice cream

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of Giuseppe's
about means the word for story is turned round

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Giuseppe tells an old story about ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TALE into ELAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is the Italian word for ice cream, now used in English.

clue.text: Exercising aplomb when eating starter of crispy hot cutlet

indicators.note: when eating means the rearranged letters take in the next pieces
exercising puts the word aplomb through its paces, moving its letters about
starter of takes the first letter of crispy

explanation.surface: A diner tackles a crispy hot cutlet with great aplomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' turns APLOMB into LAMBOP, and 'when eating' puts CH inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a small cut of lamb on the bone, a cutlet.

clue.text: Football team's filthy lucre corrupted ex-ref

indicators.note: corrupted says the letters of filthy lucre are bent out of shape

parts.note: ex- means the letters of ref are taken away

explanation.surface: A former referee was bribed with dirty money by a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges FILTHY LUCRE once 'ex-' has removed R, E, F. HULL CITY is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Hull City is a professional English club, the Tigers, based in Hull; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Military operation ordered second row in

indicators.note: in says the second row sits inside the word for ordered

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
a lock is a second-row forward in rugby union

explanation.surface: A commander orders a second row of troops in.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the two locks make up the scrum's second row.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade seals off a port or region by armed force, a military undertaking.

clue.text: I'm so aroused in fancy lace underwear

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters inside the other set
fancy works its letters into an elaborate new pattern
aroused stirs up the letters of I'm so

explanation.surface: Someone is excited by fancy lace lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'aroused' and 'fancy' are anagram signals dressed as adjectives: the stirred I'M SO goes 'in' the reworked LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless top worn as lingerie.

clue.text: Model star Ms Thurman's visiting home of tigers

indicators.note: visiting puts the actress inside the reshaped star
model as a verb means shape, so the letters of star are reshaped

parts.note: Uma Thurman is the film actress

explanation.surface: A model and the star Uma Thurman visit a place where tigers live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun beside 'star' but is the anagram signal, giving STRA; the 's of 'Ms Thurman's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island is the only habitat of the Sumatran tiger subspecies.

clue.text: Wild boy, married, that hurts wild girl without resistance

parts.note: ow is the cry for that hurts

indicators.note: wild means the remaining letters run riot
without removes the letter for resistance from girl

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A married man hurts a wild girl who offers no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes R from GIRL to leave GIL, then 'wild' rearranges it to GLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowgli is the feral child raised by wolves in Kipling's Jungle Book.

clue.text: Aphrodisiac sets Roy off

indicators.note: off means the words sets Roy go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aphrodisiac gets Roy going.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are popularly reputed to stimulate desire.

clue.text: Fitted up celebrated Republican on board

indicators.note: on board means inside, as a passenger aboard

parts.note: famed means celebrated

explanation.surface: A well-known Republican on a company board is falsely incriminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitted up' is British slang for falsely incriminated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be framed is to be falsely set up to look guilty.

clue.text: Stand-in student copper discovered bomb outside

parts.note: L is a learner driver, so a student

indicators.note: outside places the uncovered middle around copper
discovered means the word bomb has its covering ends removed

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A student police officer discovers a bomb outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' leaves OM from BOMB, which goes 'outside' CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who deputises for another.

clue.text: Underhand dealer's vehicle key?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
D sharp is a musical key

explanation.surface: A shady dealer owns a car key.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp cheats at card games, a dishonest player who deals from the bottom; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Spoiled skinned fish

indicators.note: skinned peels the outer letters off the word for spoiled

parts.note: mangled means spoiled, ruined

explanation.surface: A spoiled fish that has been skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is the verb here, not the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line.

clue.text: Business scaling fry up?

parts.note: fry are young fish, which have scales; a firm growing them into adult fish is scaling them up

explanation.surface: A company expanding its fried-food operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry up' suggests a cooked breakfast, but fry are baby fish and 'scaling up' growing them into scaled adults.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm raising trout from fry to adulthood is such a business.

clue.text: The Spanish spirit, a character unloved by Greeks

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Spanish spirit is disliked by Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon sculptures, the Elgin Marbles, to Britain; Greece wants them back.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl who took the Parthenon marbles is resented in Greece, a figure of grievance there.

clue.text: He presses all the right buttons (having a mind like a sewer!)

definitions.text: He presses all the right buttons (having a mind like a sewer!)

parts.words: He presses all the right buttons (having a mind like a sewer!)
parts.note: a seller of sewing goods pushes buttons to customers, and a sewer here is one who sews, not a drain

explanation.surface: A smooth seducer with a filthy mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain but means someone who sews; pressing buttons is selling them. A haberdasher sells sewing notions.
explanation.definitionFit: A haberdasher deals in buttons, thread and ribbons, so thinks like a seamstress.
